title: Mistral Analytics edge VPC cutover scenario notes
content:
Purpose
- Runbook-style working notes for the planned cutover of Mistral Analytics to the Redwood Private VPC/on-prem bundle. Audience: infra engineers, solutions lead, SRE. Use as source-of-truth for the cutover window and TF changes.

High-level summary
- Customer: Mistral Analytics (internal name: customer-mistral).
- Goal: Move from a hybrid cloud proof-of-concept to a fully private VPC deployment behind customer firewall with predictable throughput and a rolling upgrade plan for Redwood runtime + pinned model versions.
- Cutover window: target 2025-04-12 02:00-06:00 UTC (tentative).
- Risk profile: medium-high (first full-data private cutover for this customer).

Key constraints and assumptions
- Network: customer will provide two spine switches with 100 Gbps fabric between racks; we assume <1ms intra-rack latency. If bandwidth <40Gbps, need to re-evaluate KV cache sizing.
- Hardware: customer ordered 4 inference nodes, each 4x A100 80GB (PCIe), 1 management node (16vCPU, 128GB), 1 bastion, and a Ceph cluster with 3x NVMe servers (250TB raw). Assumption: GPU nodes expose 8 x 25GbE NICs (we plan to use 100Gb aggregated).
- Storage: Ceph cluster will be used for artifacts, model tarballs, and logs (not token KV cache). KV cache uses local NVMe on GPU nodes.
- KMS: customer uses AWS CloudHSM via VPC peering into a managed KMS endpoint. Integration requires the ri_kms terraform module to accept external key ARNs (see TF notes).
- Compliance: Data residency requires that logs are retained in-customer for 365 days.

Proposed architecture (brief)
- Network: Dedicated VPC with two subnets per AZ equivalent (control and compute). On-prem mapping: Management subnet inside customer VLAN-10, Compute inside VLAN-20. Bastion in DMZ with strict ACLs.
- Control plane: Two HA controllers (management node + secondary) running private control plane (read-only fallback via Redwood hosted control-plane disabled as per contract).
- Serving runtime: inference pool of 4 GPU nodes behind an internal load balancer. Each node runs the Redwood runtime in docker/k8s (customer prefers k8s); we will deploy as a small k8s cluster (3 master/etcd VMs are optional depending on customer k8s preference).
- Observability: Fluentd -> Ceph object storage + push metrics to customer's Prometheus endpoint. Traces forwarded to Honeycomb SaaS via dedicated egress (customer to approve).

Sizing notes (work-back numbers)
- Target SLO: 99th percentile token latency <= 450ms for interactive workloads, throughput 300 tokens/sec sustained across the fleet.
- Per-GPU throughput estimate (baseline Redwood quantized runtime, batch size 8): ~60 tokens/sec per A100-80GB.
- Required GPUs = ceil(300 / 60) = 5 GPUs -> rounding and resiliency -> 16 GPUs recommended. We currently have 4 nodes x 4 GPUs = 16 GPUs = OK for baseline.
- Headroom: +25% for burst -> capacity plan fits 16 GPUs but must implement autoscale/burst to cloud (not allowed). Therefore recommend reserving 1 node as warm spare (we plan 4 active, 1 warm spare if customer approves additional hardware).
- Memory: KV cache local writes estimated at 40GB per node active. Ensure local NVMe per node has at least 1TB usable for cache + logs.

Terraform module notes (practical)
- Modules to update/consume: ri_vpc, ri_k8s_cluster, ri_inference_pool, ri_kms, ri_monitoring, ri_tfstate-backend.
- State backend: Use central S3 bucket (redwood-terraform-state) with restricted IAM. Customer prefers on-prem object-store; we propose S3-compatible endpoint (MinIO) reachable from Redwood control plane. TF remote state path: s3://redwood-terraform-state/customers/mistral-analytics/private.
- Important TF variables required (add to customer variables file)
  - customer_id = 'mistral-analytics'
  - region = 'onprem-ny-1'
  - control_plane_ips = ['10.10.10.12', '10.10.10.13']
  - gpu_node_count = '4'
  - gpu_instance_type = 'baremetal-a100-80gb'
  - kms_key_arn = 'customer-kms-arn:...'
- State locking: use Dynamo-style lock service via Consul (customer will host) OR use S3 multipart locks. We have an ri_tfstate-locker module; customer prefers Consul. Action: confirm Consul cluster address.
- Module changes required (quick checklist):
  - ri_inference_pool: add 'node_drain_timeout' var default 300s for graceful eviction
  - ri_k8s_cluster: expose 'podDisruptionBudget' toggle for inference DaemonSet
  - ri_kms: allow external key providers (HSM path + certificate thumbprint) -> PR opened in terraform-modules PR#87 linked above
  - ri_monitoring: add 'prom_pushgateway' endpoint variable and retention days

Upgrade and cutover plan (step-by-step, draft)
- Pre-cutover (T-14 days):
  - Finalize hardware procurement and NIC firmware (customer).
  - Confirm network ACLs and egress rules (security team).
  - Run dry terraform apply to a staging VLAN provided by customer. Owner: Ana Ruiz. Due: 2025-03-20.
  - Smoke test runtime with synthetic traffic (use internal perf harness).

- T-2 days:
  - Snapshot images for all nodes, create image catalog and store in Ceph.
  - Apply ri_tfstate-backend with remote state configured and locking verified.

- Cutover day (4-hour window):
  1) Put customer POC endpoints into maintenance mode (customer side) and freeze writes to model store.
  2) Apply terraform changes for VPC + k8s cluster in incremental mode (apply ri_vpc -> ri_k8s_cluster -> ri_inference_pool). Monitor state locking.
  3) Bring up control plane nodes, ensure control-plane HA is healthy and TLS certs provisioned (certs come from customer CA).
  4) Boot GPU nodes, verify kernel/driver versions (NVIDIA driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.2) preinstalled per checklist.
  5) Deploy Redwood runtime image pinned to sha: ri-runtime:2025-02-21-sha1234 as a canary on 1 node. Run smoke inference tests.
  6) If canary is healthy for 15 minutes, rollout to remaining nodes in 1-node increments with 10 minute soak per node.
  7) Switch traffic to new private endpoints (DNS TTL pre-lowered to 30s).

- Post-cutover (T+1 day):
  - Monitor metrics for 72 hours: latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, GPU util, KV cache hit rate.
  - Retain log captures for first 48h and send to customer security for review.

Rollback strategy (if any major regression)
- If canary fails at any step, stop rollout and revert pods on the node to previous runtime (we keep previous runtime image in local registry). If issue at control plane step, fall back to POC endpoints and re-route traffic back to Redwood hosted endpoints (only if customer signed fallback option).
- Terraform: use saved plan outputs and previous state snapshots to rollback resource changes. We keep TF state snapshots in s3 path 'snapshots/<timestamp>'.

Open questions / unresolved items (ACTION REQUIRED)
- KMS/HSM details: need ciphertext examples and whether customer will allow outbound TLS to Redwood CA for key wrapping. Owner: Priya. Due: 2025-03-05.
- Consul cluster: customer to confirm availability and ACL tokens for TF locking. Owner: Ben. Due: 2025-03-01.
- Prometheus retention: default 90d on customer side. Redwood needs 30d for alerting; confirm retention mismatch.
- Will customer allow egress to Honeycomb? If not, plan to host traces in-customer (storage + retention costs).

Testing checklist (minimum)
- Kernel/driver verification script: all nodes pass nvidia-smi check -> report attached in tf-runner artifacts.
- Integration smoke tests: generate 50 concurrent sessions with average prompt length 120 tokens, ensure 99% requests return under 700ms.
- Security: run internal port-scan, ensure only required ports open (22 bastion, 443 internal LB, 2379 etcd if used).

Notes-to-self / rough TODOs (quick)
- Ana: run terraform dry-run in staging and capture apply plan (T-14d).
- Priya: finish ri_kms PR and get security signoff (T-7d).
- Jordan: prepare rollback runbook and list of tf state snapshots; test snapshot restore in dev.
- Ben: confirm Consul endpoints and lock token rotation schedule.

References and artifacts
- Perf bench results (internal): link to perf harness on GH above.
- TF modules PR#87 is the working diff for ri_kms and ri_inference_pool changes.

Appendix: example terraform variables file (customer-mistral.tfvars)
- customer_id = 'mistral-analytics'
- region = 'onprem-ny-1'
- gpu_node_count = '4'
- gpu_instance_profile = 'a100-80gb-baremetal'
- control_plane_ips = ['10.10.10.12']
- bastion_ip = '203.0.113.45'
- kms_key_arn = 'arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abcd-ef12'

End notes
- This doc is intentionally informal. Use linked artifacts for finalized runbooks. Keep a tight ship on the first 72 hours after cutover.
- Will convert to a formal runbook after we confirm Consul and KMS integration.

-- jordan
